Simulating SBML models

Source: vignettes/articles/zusbml.Rmd
zusbml.Rmd

This article takes a model from an SBML file to a simulation: reading it, looking at what it holds, deriving its equations, and running them with deSolve, events included. It ends with how the package is checked against the SBML Test Suite.

library(zusbml)

Reading a model

sbml_read() accepts a file path, a file:// or http(s):// URL, the XML as a string, or a raw vector. It reads SBML Level 3 Versions 1 and 2, and Level 2 Versions 4 and 5, which it maps to their Level 3 meaning.

m <- sbml_read(system.file("extdata", "dosing.xml", package = "zusbml"))
m
#> <sbml_model 'dosing'> SBML Level 3 Version 2
#>   compartments  2
#>   species       2
#>   parameters    3
#>   reactions     2
#>   events        1

Every element kind is a data frame, with the SBML attributes as columns in snake_case. Attributes a document leaves out are NA: Level 3 has no defaults for them.

sbml_parameters(m)[, c("id", "value", "constant")]
#>     id value constant
#> 1   ka   1.0     TRUE
#> 2   ke   0.2     TRUE
#> 3 dose 100.0     TRUE
sbml_compartments(m)[, c("id", "size", "constant")]
#>        id size constant
#> 1     gut    1     TRUE
#> 2 central   10     TRUE

Math is held as R expressions. sbml_math() shows it as R code.

sbml_math(sbml_reactions(m)$kinetic_law)
#> [1] "ka * drug_gut"       "ke * drug * central"

A document that uses an SBML Level 3 package is refused by name, with a zusbml_unsupported error; ignore_packages = TRUE reads its core model. sbml_check() reports structural problems as a data frame and never raises:

sbml_check(m)
#> [1] rule    id      message
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

Deriving the equations

sbml_odes() follows the Level 3 Version 2 specification to turn reactions and rules into states and right-hand sides:

  • a species whose symbol is an amount changes by stoichiometry times rate; one whose symbol is a concentration changes by that divided by its compartment’s size;
  • a reaction id stands for its rate, and is evaluated as an assignment;
  • function definitions and local parameters are inlined.
eq <- sbml_odes(m)
eq$states
#>       name   symbol    kind
#> 1 drug_gut drug_gut species
#> 2     drug     drug species
eq$rhs
#> $drug_gut
#> -absorption
#> 
#> $drug
#> (absorption - elimination)/central
eq$assignments
#> $absorption
#> ka * drug_gut
#> 
#> $elimination
#> ke * drug * central
eq$constants
#>     gut central      ka      ke    dose 
#>     1.0    10.0     1.0     0.2   100.0
sbml_initial_state(m)
#> drug_gut     drug 
#>      100        0

Events are carried as data:

str(eq$events[[1]][c("id", "trigger", "assignments")])
#> List of 3
#>  $ id         : chr "second_dose"
#>  $ trigger    : language time >= 12
#>  $ assignments:List of 1
#>   ..$ drug_gut: language drug_gut + dose

Simulating

sbml_derivs() returns the derivative function deSolve calls, with what else it needs as attributes: y0, the states at time 0 after any events that fire then; parms; and, for a model with events, rootfunc and events. Use lsodar, the deSolve method that finds roots.

f <- sbml_derivs(m, outputs = "absorption")
out <- deSolve::ode(
  y = attr(f, "y0"),
  times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.25),
  func = f,
  parms = attr(f, "parms"),
  method = "lsodar",
  rootfunc = attr(f, "rootfunc"),
  events = attr(f, "events")
)
plot(out[, "time"], out[, "drug"], type = "l",
     xlab = "Time (hours)", ylab = "Concentration in central")

The event engine applies the SBML rules for events: a trigger fires when it changes from false to true; initialValue says what it was before time 0; a delay postpones execution, and a non-persistent event is canceled if its trigger turns false meanwhile; events due at the same time run in priority order, in random order when tied, so set a seed for a reproducible run.

Writing

sbml_write() writes SBML Level 3 Version 2, whatever level the model was read from, and reading the result back gives the same object:

identical(sbml_read(sbml_write(m)), m)
#> [1] TRUE

sbml_to_rxode2() writes the equations as rxode2 model text. rxode2 cannot express SBML events, so events = "drop" is needed for this model:

cat(sbml_to_rxode2(m, events = "drop"))
#> # dosing, written by zusbml from SBML Level 3 Version 2
#> gut = 1;
#> central = 10;
#> ka = 1;
#> ke = 0.20000000000000001;
#> dose = 100;
#> drug_gut(0) = 100;
#> drug(0) = 0;
#> absorption = ka * drug_gut;
#> elimination = ke * drug * central;
#> d/dt(drug_gut) = -absorption;
#> d/dt(drug) = (absorption - elimination)/central;

How it is checked

The package is tested against the SBML Test Suite 3.5.0. Each of its 1,692 Level 3 Version 2 semantic cases is read, written and read back, derived, simulated with deSolve, and compared with the case’s results under its own absolute and relative tolerances. The 1,384 cases within the supported set all pass; the 308 that need algebraic rules, the delay csymbol, fast reactions or SBML packages are asserted to be refused. The 1,028 supported cases that also have a Level 2 Version 5 file pass from that file too. Fifty curated BioModels are read, round-tripped and derived in CI. Neither the suite nor the models are shipped: the suite is LGPL, and both are downloaded by scripts in the repository’s tools/ directory.
